text:
NYI visits OTT tonight with two teams that look alike on paper. Over the first six NYI games and seven OTT games, NYI has generated 2.94 expected goals per 60 and allowed 3.52, while OTT sits at 2.83 for and 2.96 against. OTT is the tighter team in its own end. At five on five, NYI has taken 49% of the expected goals and OTT 46%, so both have been outchanced more often than not. The model sees a coin flip, with 2.68 expected goals for NYI and 2.75 for OTT.

Special teams may decide it. NYI takes 5.17 penalties a game, which keeps handing the other side power plays, and its penalty kill allows 1.08 expected goals a game. OTT's kill allows 0.75, and its power play creates 0.74 a game, the same as NYI's. In net, the projected starters are Ilya Sorokin for NYI and Linus Ullmark for OTT. Sorokin is at +6.16 goals saved above expected this season (.934) and was +22.3 last year over 55 games. Ullmark is at +6.77 (.948) this season but was -13.3 last year over 49 games.

Form is a wash. Both teams are 3-2-0 in their last five with 45% of the expected goals, and each has won the chance battle in two of those games. NYI beat VAN 3-2 on Oct. 13, while OTT lost 2-7 to STL the same night after winning 4-1 at NJD the night before. For scoring, the model likes Bo Horvat (33%) and Brayden Schenn (22%) for NYI, and Tim Stützle (32%) and Drake Batherson (28%) for OTT. Stützle also has a 28% chance at two or more points.
